jobs.title: Adjunct Teaching
jobs.description: Academics Adjunct Teaching Northwest College hires qualified adjunct faculty to teach a variety of courses to meet the needs of students, both online and face-to-face (day and/or evening classes) across our service area. Applications for adjunct positions at Northwest College will ONLY be accepted via our online application system. Search for open adjunct positions here: Search for Adjunct Positions See Also: Course Descriptions Class Schedule Adjunct postings are in anticipated areas of need and do not necessarily indicate a current opening unless otherwise noted. Applicants who meet all of our qualifications for adjunct faculty will be placed into our adjunct pool and may be contacted if specific course needs necessitate hiring of an adjunct instructor. If you have questions about adjunct positions at Northwest College that are not addressed above, please contact Nancy Gilmore, Academic Affairs Administrative Secretary, at nancy.gilmore@nwc.edu.

College pays up to $2,000 for relocation expenses Start Date : As soon as feasible, Applications will be reviewed as received Salary Hire Range: $107,000 – 152,000 annually for each 12-month appointment (actual amount depends on education and experience) Job Summary: The Chief Financial Officer (CFO)/Associate Vice President (AVP) of Administrative Services has a critical role as the senior financial executive for the college and assists with the oversight of the administrative functions for the college. The position provides executive leadership, oversight, accountability, and strategic direction for the College’s financial operations. The position requires visionary leadership for the college’s financial and operational functions. The Chief Financial Officer (CFO) serves as the College’s senior financial executive and strategic advisor to the President and Board of Trustees. The position provides leadership and oversight in assigned operational areas, which may include facilities and maintenance, grounds, custodial services, transportation, safety and security, purchasing, auxiliary operations, risk management, contracts, capital projects, budgeting support, and other institutional administrative functions. The Associate Vice President works closely with the Vice President for Administrative Services and other executive leadership to support the College’s mission, strategic goals, fiscal sustainability, operational effectiveness, compliance obligations, and campus service environment. This role is in charge of budget development and execution, working capital management, financial reporting, audit coordination, internal controls, procurement, grant management, long-range financial planning, and strategic financial analysis, while ensuring compliance with Wyoming statutes, Wyoming Community College Commission (WCCC) requirements, federal regulations, and Board policy. The CFO oversees the Business Office including the Director, Accounts Payable, and Accounts Receivable. As a member of the President’s Cabinet and executive leadership team, the position plays a key leadership role in institutional planning, resource allocation, financial forecasting, operational assessment, risk management, capital planning, and organizational sustainability. The CFO is responsible for ensuring fiscal integrity, transparency, compliance, stewardship of public resources, and implementation of sound business practices across the institution. The position may serve similar duties as assigned for the Eastern Wyoming College Foundation. Incumbents will follow any other instructions, and perform any other related duties, as may be required. Description Benefits Description There is a Recruitment/Retention bonus of $14,500Position SummaryInstructional faculty has the responsibility of creating an innovative learning environment both inside and outside the classroom, and to inspire success and excellence in student learning. Examples of Duties Essential Duties and ResponsibilitiesTeach classroom, lab, and clinical components of assigned nursing and allied health courses. Collaboratively develop and implement a concept-based course plan (syllabus) in a team-based learning format. Participate in scheduled academic program reviews, including assessment of student learning at the course, program, and institutional level using feedback to make improvements. Make recommendations for textbooks and instructional resources to the faculty team. Facilitate student learning by providing a safe and supportive environment and encouraging active student participation. Demonstrate instructional competence and expertise in assigned subject matter. Use innovative instructional strategies and emerging technologies to enhance learning. Facilitate distance education delivery and provide support to outreach students. Apply knowledge of diverse communities and skill sets to customize effective teaching methods. Assess student learning and performance, and provide formative feedback in a timely manner. Maintain accurate and complete course records, relay student engagement information, and enter final grades in accordance within established deadlines. Foster effective working relationships with the healthcare team to provide a comprehensive and safe environment for students’ clinical learning experiences. Work with clinical preceptors to develop an instructional plan outlining clinical learning experiences, and to assess students’ clinical performance. Function as a role model for professional nursing and communicate this role to students. Share pertinent student information with colleagues, including but not limited to progress reports, attendance records, and academic difficulty issues. Assist students with degree planning and conduct regularly scheduled advisement sessions to discuss progress toward achieving learning outcomes. Provide a workload schedule showing instructional and office hours. Oversee the efficient use of supplies and equipment in the campus lab and clinical area; make purchase recommendations to the nursing director. Assist with positive program promotion and recruitment. Attend program advisory board and college meetings as required. Fulfill responsibilities in accordance with institutional policies and procedures in a professional manner. Assume responsibility for professional development, service to the college, and other reasonably related duties as needed. Typical Qualifications Minimum Qualifications EducationBachelor’s degree in nursing from a regionally accredited institution of higher learning recognized by the U.S. Department of Education. Must submit an approved education plan and complete a graduate degree in nursing within five years of hire. Experience Three years of nursing experience with a strong preference for recent work in direct patient care. Licenses/Certifications Unencumbered license to practice professional nursing in the State of Wyoming, or the ability to obtain licensure within two months of hire.
